body: @nomad-vagabond Thanks for reporting this issue. I tried to reproduce it [here](https://issues.streamlit.app/?issue=gh-7813) and the iframe background color is whatever color is configured in the theme. But I think this was always the case, we haven't really changed anything related to the Iframe in `1.29`. Do you have a more specific reproducible snippet related to your case? Why do you need it to be transparent?

Hello, this issue occurred in my app as well. I noticed when I updated & rebuilt it today. It works fine in Streamlit `v1.28.2`, but not in Streamlit `v1.29.0`. ### Here's steps for reproducing what happens in my app Using Streamlit `v1.29.0`, opened in Google Chrome `119.0.6045.200`. In `.streamlit/config.toml`: ``` [theme] backgroundColor="#2d4786" ``` In `page.py`: ``` st.title("Test") js = """ """ st.components.v1.html(js) ``` Screenshot of `page.py`: ![image](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/assets/7428799/ba9d907c-4825-4966-9d1d-af30ee573f32) In the HTML code, a wrapped iframe is created with the following code: ```html
``` Sizes of the HTML elements: - The script is located in the iframe's document head. - The iframe's document body has size `688 x 0`. - The iframe has size `750 x 150`, which matches exactly the white background size. - The wrapper has size `750 x 157.594`. Dirty fix: - Setting `backgroundColor: #2d4786` on the iframe does not do anything. - Setting `backgroundColor: #2d4786` on the iframe's document body fills the white background. When comparing the HTML code with what's generated in the previous (`v1.28.2`), the only change I see is the `e1f1d6gn3` class in `v1.28.2`, becoming `e1f1d6gn4` class in `v1.29.0`. I have no clue on the background or any CSS rule changing.

Thanks for the additional information. I was able to reproduce the issue with Firefox and Safari, but not with Chrome. The root cause of the issue seems to be the `color-scheme: dark` property that is added to Streamlit for apps with dark backgrounds. I started with a fix for this here: https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/7821

issue.body:
## Describe your changes

This PR fixes an issue with iframes where the background uses white instead of transparent if a dark background is configured. This only happens in Firefox and Safari; Chrome uses the correct background.

The reason is that we recently added the `color-schema` keyword to indicate the browser if the app is in dark or light mode. But this triggers an automatic behavior where the browsers adds a white background to iframes since it assumes that the iframe can only handle a light background. We have to tell the iframe that the iframe supports both `light` and `dark` color schemes to fix this. 

## GitHub Issue Link (if applicable)

- Closes https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/7813

## Testing Plan

- Migrates e2e components test to playwright to also cover firefox and safari browsers.
